record.paper_title: Momentum–energy of the non-radiating electromagnetic field: open problems?
record.context_brief: Bound-field energy flux for an isolated charge
record.original_question: In classical electrodynamics, for the bound electromagnetic field of a single point-like charge moving with constant velocity, can one formulate a mathematically consistent local energy-balance law and corresponding definition of field energy flux and momentum after removing self-action, in a way that does not force the pair consisting of the field energy density u and the field energy-flux density S to transform as a four-vector when the bound field is instead treated as part of a symmetric tensor? Equivalently, which description of bound-field energy transport is physically correct in this setting: the standard Poynting-vector description or the Umov-vector description in which the field energy moves rigidly with the charge?

evidence.quote: Thus, equation (23) is transformed into the form (30), which does not contain any infinite terms, and further renormalization is not required. The only problem is that the expression vEu (Umov’s vector) and the Poynting vector SE give quite different physical interpretation for the energy flux. In particular, equation (30) tells us that the energy of EM field of charged particle rigidly moves in space together with the particle. On the other hand, the Poynting vector gives essentially more complex picture for the energy flaw. In the author’s opinion, the difference in physical interpretation of equations (23) and (30) represents one of open problems of classical electrodynamics.

We have shown that the energy balance equation for this particle ∂u/∂t + ∇ · SE = 0, obtained from the Poynting theorem after cancellation of the self-action term EEs · Ej, is mathematically incorrect. Indeed, the latter equality represents a sufficient condition that the variables u and SE constitute a four-vector. However, it is known that the energy density u and flux density SE for a bound-EM field represent not a four-vector, but the time-like components of a symmetric tensor. ... It seems that a resolution of this contradictory situation cannot be simply done ... and it represents an open problem of classical electrodynamics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider, in Minkowski spacetime with metric signature (+,-,-,-), the classical electromagnetic field produced by a single isolated point charge q moving with constant velocity v. Let E(x,t) and B(x,t) denote the bound (Liénard–Wiechert) electric and magnetic fields of this charge, and define

  u(x,t) = (1/8π)(|E|^2 + |B|^2),    S_E(x,t) = (c/4π) E × B,

the standard electromagnetic energy density and Poynting flux. Subtracting the divergent self-action contribution from the Poynting energy-balance identity formally yields a renormalized local conservation law of the form

  ∂u/∂t + ∇ · S = 0,                                (★)

for some renormalized flux S. Two candidate fluxes appear in the literature for the bound field of a uniformly moving charge:
  (i) the Poynting vector S = S_E;
  (ii) the Umov vector S = u v, expressing that the field energy is convected rigidly with the charge.

Now note the following tension. If (★) holds as a genuine local conservation law with u and S forming the time-like components (T^{00}, T^{0i}) of a symmetric, divergence-free energy–momentum tensor T^{μν} of the bound field, then (u, S/c) need not transform as a four-vector under Lorentz boosts; whereas equation (★) by itself, treated as a scalar continuity equation, is a sufficient condition forcing (u, S/c) to transform as a four-vector, contradicting the tensorial character of T^{μν}.

Problem. Formulate, for the bound electromagnetic field of a single point charge in uniform motion and after a mathematically well-defined removal of self-action, a consistent local energy-balance law together with an unambiguous definition of the renormalized field energy density u and energy flux S such that:
  (a) the law is compatible with (u, S/c) being the time-like components of a symmetric, divergence-free energy–momentum tensor (rather than a four-vector);
  (b) it determines uniquely which of the two candidate fluxes — the Poynting vector S_E or the Umov vector u v — correctly describes the transport of bound-field energy in this setting, or otherwise specifies the correct flux.

Decide which description is physically and mathematically correct, and exhibit the corresponding consistent renormalization scheme; or prove that no such formulation exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface any subsequent work claiming a definitive resolution of the inconsistency between the Poynting-vector and Umov-vector descriptions of the bound-field energy transport for a uniformly moving charge after self-action removal. The question appears to remain an open conceptual/foundational issue in classical electrodynamics, with no widely accepted resolution identified.
